title: Effectiveness of a Generate→Validate→Repair Pipeline with Batfish for Intent-to-Configuration Translation: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (CNSM2026-GenVal-Batfish-PR-v1) to test whether inserting a deterministic Batfish-style validator into a bounded generate→validate→repair pipeline reduces validator-detected deployment-risk configuration errors from an LLM intent-to-configuration translator. Crucially, the preregistered execution contract used shared_initial_generation (one initial model generation per task reused for both baseline and guarded scoring), so the primary estimand detects only improvements that arise from validator-triggered repairs and not differences due to independent model stochasticity. Under that contract we executed 200 paired tasks (50 per stratum: IOS-like vs JunOS-like × single-step vs multi-step) using the declared model gpt-5-mini and a bounded repair budget (≤1 repair/apply attempt per task). All archived artifacts show both arms were validator-clean on every task (baseline = 200/200, guarded = 200/200), giving observed paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples; seed archived) and exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. No repairs were invoked (repair count = 0), so the preregistered secondary estimand (repair_success_rate > 50%) is not empirically computable. We report artifact-backed reconciliation of these degenerate outcomes, summarize the deterministic validator semantics used to define the primary outcome, and discuss construct-, internal-, and external-validity implications and follow-up sensitivity designs.

sections.introduction: Translating operator intent into device configuration can accelerate network operations but risks unsafe changes that violate reachability, policy, routing, or interface-state invariants. A common mitigation architecture is a generate→validate→repair workflow that places a deterministic verifier (Batfish-style) in the loop and optionally issues automated repairs or human approvals. Prior work prototypes such workflows and advocates layered controls, but there is limited preregistered, paired evidence that isolates the marginal verifier benefit under a bounded repair budget and a fixed estimand. We therefore asked: Does integrating a deterministic Batfish-like validator into a bounded generate→validate→repair pipeline reduce validator-detected deployment-risk configuration errors relative to one-shot LLM generation? Contributions: (1) a sealed preregistered paired confirmatory design (n=200) and a single primary estimand focused on the verifier marginal effect; (2) an automated execution of the bounded generate→validate→repair adapter (hosted_netops_gvr_v1) using gpt-5-mini under a shared_initial_generation contract (one shared initial candidate per task, reused by both arms), which isolates repair-induced differences from generation variance; (3) an artifact-backed empirical outcome (zero discordant pairs), a concise description of the deterministic validator semantics that define the primary outcome, and a focused discussion of implications and follow-ons given the degenerate confirmatory result.
sections.related_work: Recent literature documents active interest in LLMs for NetOps tasks and proposes verifier-in-the-loop and bounded self-correction patterns. Representative empirical and system-level works include intent-driven configuration pipelines (Nguyen Tu et al., 2024), intent-translation prototypes (Wei et al., ICNP 2025), and meta-reasoning/repair frameworks (Sang, ICMLCA 2025). Surveys and position papers emphasize workflow-centred evaluation, layered controls (human gates, sandboxing, traceability), and the need for taxonomies of failure modes in agentic systems. While many prototypes argue for verifier-assisted correction, published evaluations often report prototype-level results or position arguments rather than preregistered, paired trials that isolate the marginal verifier contribution under a bounded repair budget.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design: We preregistered CNSM2026-GenVal-Batfish-PR-v1 (sealed) with a paired binary design (200 tasks, 2 conditions per task: baseline vs guarded). Tasks: 200 synthetic intent-to-configuration tasks balanced across four strata (50 tasks each: IOS-like single-step, IOS-like multi-step, JunOS-like single-step, JunOS-like multi-step) as specified in the preregistration and archived task manifest. Model and pipeline: declared model = gpt-5-mini; adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1 implementing a bounded generate→validate→repair transformation with maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1. Execution contract: shared_initial_generation (one initial generation per task was produced and reused for both conditions), intentionally constraining detectable differences to repairs applied after validator detection rather than to independent generator stochasticity. Analysis plan: primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; primary test = exact McNemar two-sided (α=0.05); uncertainty quantified by a paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples). The full preregistered sampling, missingness, multiplicity, and sensitivity plans are archived with the preregistration.
sections.results: Execution and scoring (artifact-backed): planned episodes = 400 (200 tasks × 2 conditions); completed episodes = 400; failed episodes = 0; provider_call accounting recorded hosted_model_call_event_count = 200 consistent with shared_initial_generation and the adapter contract. Condition summaries: baseline validator-clean = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0); guarded validator-clean = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0). Paired contingency: n_11 = 200, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed archived) = [0.0, 0.0]; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Repair activity: zero tasks triggered a repair (repair count = 0); therefore the preregistered secondary estimand (repair_success_rate) is not computable from these data. Representative per-episode scoring artifacts and aggregated analysis artifacts (contingency table, condition summary, reconciliation) are archived in the execution bundle. For readers judging task challenge: strata counts are 50 tasks per preregistered stratum; the task generator annotated representative examples with difficulty labels (representative sample: medium = 1/6, hard = 2/6, very_hard = 3/6); full per-task labels and the full task manifest are archived for inspection.
sections.discussion: Statistical and construct interpretation: the observed data are degenerate for the primary estimand because there were no discordant pairs—both arms returned validator-clean configurations for every task. Under the shared_initial_generation contract this outcome indicates that (a) the single shared initial candidate per task satisfied the deterministic validator for the supplied synthetic task bank and (b) no validator-triggered repairs were invoked. This empirical null does not imply verifier-in-the-loop defenses lack value more broadly. Important design and construct limits that reduce detectable marginal verifier benefit: (1) shared_initial_generation suppressed generation variance, therefore any verifier benefit that would have arisen only through a different sampled generation per arm cannot be observed; (2) the synthetic task corpus is template-aligned and may under-challenge the generator; (3) only a single model family (gpt-5-mini) and a single bounded repair iteration (≤1) were tested; (4) the deterministic_netops_validator_v5 approximates Batfish semantics in sandbox scenarios but cannot reproduce all production-device quirks. Recommended follow-ups (consistent with preregistered sensitivity plans): run independent_condition_generation (separate draws per arm) to reintroduce generator variance; expand repair budget to iterative repairs (≥2) and measure repair-success rates; test multiple model families and temperatures; increase task heterogeneity and adversarial scenarios; evaluate richer verifier environments including device-in-the-loop emulation. These follow-ups are precisely the dimensions that determine when verifier-assisted repairs become measurable.
sections.conclusion: We executed a sealed preregistered paired trial of a bounded generate→validate→repair workflow (gpt-5-mini + deterministic Batfish-style validator) on 200 synthetic intent-to-configuration tasks under a shared_initial_generation contract. Both arms were validator-clean on every task (200/200), yielding an observed paired difference of 0.0 (paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.0]) and McNemar p = 1.0. No repairs were invoked, so the preregistered repair-success hypothesis could not be evaluated. The degenerate null outcome highlights that execution contracts (shared vs independent generation), task-bank difficulty and template alignment, model choice, and verifier expressiveness jointly determine whether verifier-assisted repairs are empirically observable; future preregistered trials should vary these axes to identify regimes with measurable verifier benefit. All preregistration and execution/analysis artifacts are archived to enable exact reproduction and targeted follow-on preregistered experiments.

limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to a synthetic, public task corpus and a deterministic Batfish-like sandbox; results do not generalize to production devices, multi-vendor heterogeneity, or richer harm oracles.
Single model family tested (gpt-5-mini) and a single bounded repair budget (≤1 repair); no cross-model or multi-iteration repair claims are made.

Preregistered shared_initial_generation (independent_condition_generation=false) produced one shared initial generation per task that was reused for both conditions; this reduces sensitivity to generator stochasticity and therefore reduces the likelihood of observing discordant pairs arising purely from generation variance.

The repair loop was never invoked because baseline produced zero validator-detected errors; therefore the preregistered secondary hypothesis about repair-success (>50%) could not be empirically evaluated.

Contamination and template-alignment risk: automated contamination checks recorded no flagged items, but pretraining memorization or template-alignment remains a construct-validity threat that automated checks cannot fully eliminate.
Adversarial and prompt-injection scenarios were not included; the study does not assess robustness under targeted attacks.
